title: UNIT 1: CHEMISTRY AND ITS IMPORTANCE
notes:
✓ Chemistry → the branch of science that studies matter, its composition, structure, properties and the changes it undergoes.

✓ Chemistry is important in medicine, agriculture, food production, manufacturing, energy, environmental protection and many other areas of society.

title: 1.1 Definition and Scope of Chemistry
notes:
✓ Chemistry → the scientific study of matter and the changes that matter undergoes.

◆ Chemistry studies:
✓ Composition → what a substance is made of.
✓ Structure → how atoms and molecules are arranged.
✓ Properties → characteristics of substances.
✓ Reactions → how substances change into new substances.
✓ Energy → energy absorbed or released during chemical changes.

→ Chemistry connects microscopic particles such as atoms and molecules with materials and processes observed in everyday life.

title: 1.1.1 Matter
notes:
✓ Matter → anything that has mass and occupies space.

◆ Matter exists mainly as:
✓ Solid → definite shape and volume.
✓ Liquid → definite volume but no definite shape.
✓ Gas → no definite shape or volume.

→ Matter can undergo physical changes, such as melting, or chemical changes, such as combustion.

title: 1.1.2 Substance
notes:
✓ A substance → a form of matter with a definite composition and characteristic properties.

◆ Examples:
✓ Water → H₂O.
✓ Oxygen → O₂.
✓ Sodium chloride → NaCl.

→ Substances may be elements or compounds.

title: 1.1.3 Composition
notes:
✓ Composition → the types and relative amounts of particles or elements present in a substance.

✓ Example:
Water consists of hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed ratio of 2:1.

→ Composition helps identify and distinguish different substances.

title: 1.1.4 Structure
notes:
✓ Structure → how atoms, ions or molecules are arranged and bonded in a substance.

→ The structure of a substance strongly affects its physical and chemical properties.

◆ Example:
Diamond and graphite are both made of carbon, but their different structures give them very different properties.

title: 1.1.5 Property
notes:
✓ Property → a characteristic of a substance that can be observed or measured.

◆ Physical properties:
✓ Color.
✓ Density.
✓ Melting point.
✓ Boiling point.
✓ Electrical conductivity.

✓ Chemical properties → describe how a substance reacts with other substances.

title: 1.1.6 Energy
notes:
✓ Energy → the capacity to do work or cause change.

◆ Chemical reactions may:
✓ Release energy → exothermic process.
✓ Absorb energy → endothermic process.

→ Chemistry studies energy changes in reactions and applies them in fuels, batteries, food, industrial processes and other technologies.

title: 1.2 Chemistry and Other Natural Sciences
notes:
✓ Chemistry is closely related to other natural sciences.

◆ Physics → studies energy, forces and physical behavior of matter.
◆ Biology → uses chemistry to understand cells, metabolism and life processes.
◆ Geology → uses chemistry to study minerals, rocks and Earth's materials.
◆ Environmental science → applies chemistry to pollution, water and air quality.
◆ Medicine → uses chemistry to understand drugs and biological processes.

title: 1.3 Chemistry in Production and Society
notes:
✓ Chemistry plays an important role in producing useful materials and improving quality of life.

◆ Applications include:
✓ Medicines and healthcare.
✓ Fertilizers and agricultural chemicals.
✓ Food preservation and processing.
✓ Construction materials.
✓ Fuels and energy.
✓ Plastics and polymers.
✓ Metals and alloys.
✓ Soaps and detergents.
✓ Water treatment.

title: 1.3.1 Chemical Industry
notes:
✓ Chemical industry → uses chemical processes and raw materials to manufacture useful chemical products on a large scale.

◆ Products include:
✓ Fertilizers.
✓ Cement and construction chemicals.
✓ Pharmaceuticals.
✓ Paints.
✓ Plastics.
✓ Soaps and detergents.
✓ Pesticides.
✓ Industrial gases.

title: 1.3.2 Chemical Products
notes:
✓ Chemical products → substances manufactured or processed for useful purposes.

◆ Examples include:
✓ Medicines.
✓ Fertilizers.
✓ Detergents.
✓ Plastics.
✓ Paints.
✓ Cosmetics.
✓ Pesticides.
✓ Fuels.

→ Many everyday products depend on chemical knowledge and industrial processes.

title: 1.3.3 Analgesics
notes:
✓ Analgesics → medicines used to relieve or reduce pain without necessarily causing loss of consciousness.

◆ Examples include paracetamol and ibuprofen.

→ They are commonly used for headaches, muscle pain, fever-related discomfort and other mild to moderate pain.

title: 1.3.4 Antibiotics
notes:
✓ Antibiotics → medicines that kill bacteria or inhibit their growth.

→ They are used to treat bacterial infections and do not normally treat viral infections such as the common cold.

◆ Examples include penicillin and amoxicillin.

✓ Responsible use is important because inappropriate antibiotic use can contribute to antibiotic resistance.

title: 1.3.5 Anesthetics
notes:
✓ Anesthetics → substances used to produce loss of sensation, especially pain, during medical or surgical procedures.

◆ Types include:
✓ Local anesthetics → numb a specific area.
✓ General anesthetics → produce unconsciousness during major procedures.

title: 1.3.6 Antiseptics
notes:
✓ Antiseptics → chemical substances applied to living tissues such as skin to reduce or prevent the growth of microorganisms.

◆ Examples include some iodine preparations and chlorhexidine products.

→ They help reduce the risk of infection in wounds and during medical procedures.

title: 1.3.7 Disinfectants
notes:
✓ Disinfectants → chemical substances used on non-living surfaces to destroy or reduce harmful microorganisms.

◆ Examples include chlorine-based disinfectants and some alcohol-based products.

◆ REMEMBER
✓ Antiseptic → used on living tissue.
✓ Disinfectant → used mainly on non-living surfaces.

title: 1.3.8 Insecticides
notes:
✓ Insecticides → substances used to kill, control or repel harmful insects.

→ They are important in agriculture and public health because they can help control crop pests and disease-carrying insects.

✓ They should be used carefully to reduce harm to humans, beneficial organisms and the environment.

title: 1.3.9 Tranquilizers
notes:
✓ Tranquilizers → medicines that reduce anxiety, tension or agitation and may produce a calming effect.

→ They act on the central nervous system and should be used only as directed by a qualified healthcare professional because some can cause dependence or other harmful effects.

title: 1.3.10 Metallurgy
notes:
✓ Metallurgy → the science and technology of extracting metals from ores, refining them and preparing useful metal products and alloys.

◆ Main stages may include:
✓ Ore concentration.
✓ Extraction or reduction.
✓ Refining.
✓ Alloy production.

→ Metallurgy is important in construction, transportation, machinery and manufacturing.

title: 1.4 Common Chemical Industries in Ethiopia
notes:
✓ Chemical industries in Ethiopia contribute to agriculture, construction, manufacturing, healthcare and consumer products.

◆ Important areas include:
✓ Cement and construction materials.
✓ Fertilizer and agricultural inputs.
✓ Pharmaceuticals.
✓ Soap and detergent production.
✓ Paint and coatings.
✓ Plastics and related products.
✓ Food and beverage processing.
✓ Textile and leather chemical processing.

→ These industries transform raw materials into useful products and support economic development and employment.

title: UNIT 1 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
✓ Chemistry → study of matter, its composition, structure, properties and changes.
✓ Matter → anything with mass and volume.
✓ Substance → matter with definite composition and characteristic properties.
✓ Composition → what a substance contains.
✓ Structure → arrangement and bonding of particles.
✓ Property → characteristic of a substance.
✓ Energy → capacity to cause change or do work.

✓ Analgesic → relieves pain.
✓ Antibiotic → treats bacterial infections.
✓ Anesthetic → causes loss of sensation.
✓ Antiseptic → reduces microorganisms on living tissue.
✓ Disinfectant → reduces microorganisms on non-living surfaces.
✓ Insecticide → controls insects.
✓ Tranquilizer → produces a calming effect.
✓ Metallurgy → extraction, refining and processing of metals.

◆ EXAM TIP
✓ Antiseptic → living tissue.
✓ Disinfectant → non-living surface.
✓ Analgesic → pain relief.
✓ Antibiotic → bacteria.
✓ Anesthetic → loss of sensation.
